title: PNP on ex-Sara Duterte staff members: No rescue, release happened because they were not 'held'
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday clarified that there was "no rescue or release" of a former household staff member of Vice President Sara Duterte and four other individuals.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday clarified that there was "no rescue or release" of a former household staff member of Vice President Sara Duterte and four other individuals.
In a statement, the PNP pointed out that the concerned ex-former staff members of Duterte were not being held captive when police accompanied their lawyers to a hotel in Taguig City on November 17.
"There was no rescue and no release, because no one was being held," the PNP said.
Patay ang tatlong lalaki matapos mabagsakan ng tangke ng tubig sa Abulug, Cagayan.
On Wednesday, Duterte’s camp said that two of her former staff members who allegedly received threats to their lives were already safe and sound following a rescue operation with the help of police.

Duterte's spokesperson, Atty. Paolo Panelo, said the two former staff members were recruited by a private individual to work at a resort in Boracay in October. They were later brought to Manila under the pretext of training for their jobs.
Panelo claimed that their employer told them that the threats against them would be quelled if they signed affidavits containing allegations against the Vice President, which they refused to sign.
Duterte is currently facing an impeachment trial in the Senate.

According to the PNP, two legal counsels went to Fort Bonifacio Police Sub-Station 1 in Taguig on November 17 and requested police assistance in fetching a former Duterte staff member and four other individuals from a hotel in Bonifacio Global City.
Police personnel accompanied the lawyers and found the five individuals, who were not restrained and did not report any immediate threat to their safety.
All five came down from their hotel rooms on their own and went with the police officers to the station, the PNP said.

“At the station, the individuals declined to execute affidavits regarding their reported captivity and did not identify anyone allegedly involved or disclose the source of the supposed threats,” the PNP said.
“Their legal counsels instead executed and submitted an affidavit for documentation, which became the basis for the police blotter dated November 17, 2026,” it added.
After the documentation, the five individuals left the station without raising any further concern or requesting additional assistance, according to the PNP.
The PNP said it remains ready to receive complaints and sworn statements and provide appropriate police assistance and protection to anyone reporting threats.
But it also reiterated its commitment to remain apolitical and carry out its mandate fairly and impartially, regardless of political affiliations or differences. —VAL, GMA News
